title: Hosted + Dedicated: Quarantine Flow for Partial Region Degradation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: In the last two cross-region incidents we observed partial degradation in a single region where a subset of tenants experienced elevated tail latency and KV cache desynchronization. Existing full-region failover is heavyweight for short-lived degradations and causes capacity churn for Dedicated pools. This ticket defines a lightweight, automated quarantine flow that (1) isolates affected tenants to reduce blast radius, (2) routes their traffic to a protected warm-path while preserving SLA for unaffected tenants, and (3) attempts KV cache stitch/repair before executing full tenant rehome. The flow must work for both Hosted API and Dedicated tenant pools and be operable by on-call within the Console or via CLI API calls.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can mark a tenant as 'quarantined' via Console and API; Console button and CLI command exist
Quarantined traffic is routed to a configurable warm-path (same-region or remote) with weight and concurrency caps
Automatic KV cache reconciliation attempts start immediately after quarantine; success triggers rejoin without rehome
If reconciliation fails within configurable timeout, system triggers controlled rehome to warm pool or alternate region with tenant priority preserved
Runbook includes post-action alerts, rollback instructions, and a checklist for customer communications
Playbook validated in staging with injected partial-region degradation and a dedicated-tenant testbed
runbook_steps: Detect: Oncall receives Alert 'region-REDACT partial degradation' and dashboard shows tenant latency spike > 3x p95 for 5m
Triage: Confirm affected tenant list via query 'tenant.latency > baseline' and 'kv-miss-rate' dashboard slice
Quarantine: In Console, select tenant -> Actions -> Quarantine. Alternatively run CLI: redwoodctl tenant quarantine --tenant <id> --reason 'partial-region-deg'
Traffic Shift: Quarantine flow applies egress policy: set route weight 0.1 to original pool, 0.9 to warm-path or remote compatible model variant; concurrency cap 10 per tenant
KV Reconciliation: Trigger KV repair job: redwoodctl kv reconcile --tenant <id> --mode incremental; monitor 'kv-stitch-success' metric
Monitor: If kv-stitch-success metric > 90% and latency returns to baseline for 3 consecutive 1m windows, issue 'Rejoin' action to remove quarantine
Escalation: If kv-stitch not complete after timeout (default 15m), execute Controlled Rehome: schedule rehome to warm pool with rolling connection drain and tenant priority preservation
Customer comms: Use template 'quarantine-notice' to notify affected accounts; update support ticket with links to quarantine audit and mitigation steps
Cleanup: After rejoin or rehome, run post-checks (cache consistency, request success rate) and annotate runbook execution in incident tracker
rollback_steps: If quarantine causes unexpected side-effects (e.g., warm-path overload): revert weights to pre-action values and pause new quarantines
If rehome introduces higher error rate, immediately rollback to previous tenant placement and open emergency scale request for warm pool
Document rollback in incident ticket and create follow-up action to refine warm-path capacity thresholds
telemetry_checks: Thresholds: tenant p95 > 3x baseline for 5m triggers triage
SLO gates: post-rejoin success requires error rate < 0.5% and p95 within 1.25x baseline for 10m
Health metrics to watch during quarantine: warm-path CPU/GPU util < 70%, rpc-error-rate < 1%
postmortem_actions: Add automated detection rule for the exact latency + kv-miss signature that led to this incident
Tune default quarantine timeout and warm-path capacity based on staging experiments
Create a small runbook training session for oncall with recorded demo and tabletop exercise
Implement a conservative throttling policy for Dedicated warm-pools to avoid cold overload
